title: Physical Therapy & Sports Rehab Cleaning Standards Guide
heroTitle: Physical Therapy & Sports Rehab Facility Cleaning Guide
heroSubtitle: Sanitization protocols for athletic turf, treatment mats, weight stations, and hydrotherapy wet rooms.
metaDescription: Guide to physical therapy facility cleaning, synthetic turf antimicrobial extraction, non-slip floor safety (ASTM D2047), and equipment disinfection.

sections.title: Infection Control in Rehabilitation Environments
sections.content: Physical therapy patients are frequently recovering from joint replacement or orthopedic surgery. High-touch rehab equipment, exercise mats, and turf surfaces must be sanitized daily to prevent healthcare-associated infections.

sections.title: Non-Slip Hard Flooring & Patient Fall Prevention
sections.content: Rehab facility floors must maintain high slip resistance under ASTM D2047 standards. Cleaning products must remove sweat and moisture without leaving slick residues that pose fall hazards for patients.

calloutContent: Learn how XIRI maintains slip-coefficient logs and antimicrobial turf extraction for physical therapy clinics.

faqs.question: How often should athletic turf be extracted in a physical therapy clinic?
faqs.answer: Low-moisture antimicrobial extraction should be performed 2x per week in high-traffic rehab zones to eliminate sweat and bacterial buildup.
